title: Design strategies and elements of building envelope for urban acoustic environment

findings.antecedent: densely populated high-rise buildings with a hard reflective façade built from glass, stone, and metal
findings.consequent: ambient noise levels in urban acoustic environments
findings.quote: In particular, densely populated high-rise buildings with a hard reflective façade built from glass, stone, and metal are the main causes of increased ambient noise levels [10] in

findings.antecedent: appropriate architectural design of a building envelope
findings.consequent: noise level acoustically and soundscape perceivably
findings.quote: An appropriate architectural design of a building envelope can significantly reduce the noise level acoustically and improve soundscape perceivably.

findings.antecedent: geometric and material building envelope design elements
findings.quote: A meta-analysis of noise abatement demonstrated that geometric and material building envelope design elements can reduce outdoor noise levels.
Vegetation on building envelopes has been found to have good performance in both noise abatement and soundscape performance.

findings.consequent: specular sound reflections and outdoor noise levels
findings.quote: The textured surfaces can increase surface roughness, and the fragmented surfaces can enhance edge diffraction. ... Building envelopes should not comprise a single flat surface to minimize strong specular sound reflections, which increase outdoor noise levels.

findings.antecedent: protrusions of the building envelope (balconies, eaves, louvres, screens, roof solar panels)
findings.quote: The protrusions of the building envelope, such as eaves [77], louvres [76,80,99], screens [39,51,64,79], and roof solar panels [95] can reduce specular sound reflections owing to their geometric shape.

findings.antecedent: protrusions combined with sound absorbing material
findings.quote: When these protrusions were combined with the sound absorbing material, the insertion loss could increase.

findings.antecedent: lower building height and wider street
findings.consequent: road traffic noise on the street
findings.quote: The lower the building height and the wider the street, the less the road traffic noise on the street.
The more absorbing materials, the more the insertion loss.
The vegetation can be considered as a type of material which gives textured surface and is sound absorptive.
Green walls and green roofs are known to exhibit high thermal performances [113,114].
Vegetation exerts multisensory effects on human perception.

findings.antecedent: green views and fragrance of blossoms
findings.quote: green views [82,94] and fragrance of blossoms [97] reduced the noise annoyance in urban areas.

findings.consequent: short-term recovery from stress or mental fatigue and faster physical recovery from illnesses
findings.quote: Green spaces facilitate the short-term recovery from stress or mental fatigue and provide faster physical recovery from illnesses [115].
Green environments are rated as more thermally comfortable than water and built environments [116].
Vegetation can significantly improve environmental noise perception [117].
Multisensory designs can help to improve human environ- mental perception in general.

findings.antecedent: positive auditory stimuli, visual factors, thermal comfort, and olfactory factors
findings.consequent: soundscape quality, acoustic comfort, and noise annoyance
